# SEO-231: Exclude the largest visible image from lazy loading

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

Images below the initial viewport defer their load, while the image most likely to be the largest element visible on arrival loads eagerly and is not deferred by a lazy-loading attribute or a script-based loader.

## Rationale

Deferring the image the reader is waiting for delays the moment the page appears finished, so applying the attribute uniformly across a template makes the most important image the slowest one.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_images"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Identify the hero or leading image per template and opt it out of the deferring attribute explicitly, rather than applying the attribute in a shared component with no exception. Verify per template, because which image leads differs between them.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Measure which element is the largest painted in the viewport on load and confirm it is not among the images marked for deferred loading.
- Evidence: `BROWSER`, `PERFORMANCE_MEASUREMENT`, `RENDERED_HTML`
- Automated check: none.
